arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Ainsa argued the general statute waives sovereign immunity for third parties.
Ms. Maynard argued specific remedies foreclose general remedies when purposes conflict.
Justice Roberts asked how strict construction of immunity waivers applies here.
Justice Ginsburg asked why a prior case noted the specific statute was unavailable.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case involves a trust seeking a tax refund. The trust argues a general statute allows its suit. The government argues a specific statute controls and blocks the suit.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on February 26, 2007.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The trust wants the Court to allow its refund suit under the general statute.
The government wants the Court to block the suit because the specific statute controls.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The trust argues the general statute waives sovereign immunity for third parties.
The government argues the specific statute forecloses the general remedy.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Kennedy asked if the specific-over-general principle applies in tax law.
Justice Stevens asked if the two statutes serve separate functions regarding collection and amount.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines if third parties can sue for refunds under general statutes. It affects how taxpayers challenge government tax collections. It clarifies the scope of sovereign immunity waivers in tax disputes.
